newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India volatile, ends slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India volatile, ends slightly lower.

text.p: The GDR market slipped lower but remained volatile on Wednesday, as traders recovered from a short-lived flurry at the start of the week and began to square their books for the year-end. "It was an interesting day, the local market was weaker but there were some buyers around for Hindalco and East India Hotels," said a trader. "There was definitely some bottom fishing and there is no doubt that the market is cheap. But with Hong Kong and the U.S. there is not a huge interest in India and there's a lot of stock around."
The market bounced through the day but closed only slightly lower, and traders see little more serious activity before the end of the year.
The Cazenove Indian GDR Index was off 1.12 points or 1.66 percent at 66.52 after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 62.30 points or 2.11 percent to end at a provisional 2886.14.
Indian blue chip GDRs were mixed with Grasim, Indian Hotels, Hindalco and Reliance marginally higher but Tata and Bajaj Auto slipping further after two days of gains.
Elsewhere, Lebanon's biggest company Solidere issued 6.16 million GDRs worth $77 million.

Traders said they had heard of the deal, lead by Merrill Lynch. "It was a small deal, quite tight and priced low," said one. "Merrill was supporting it at about $11.50. But there was not much interest from anyone else."
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI was at 58.96 at 1612 GMT, down 0.43 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.76 percent compared with yesterday's 16.70 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended at 65.23, up 0.67 percent with a premium of 29.50 percent over the local market. The Capel Taiwan GDR Index was off 0.62 percent at 95.45.
